content.jointProblem: What explains the apparent manganese increase across AquaCikl’s treatment process and its iron non-compliance, and could an operational change restore compliance without major equipment replacement? The first experiment would test whether Radulović’s groundwater analytical methods transfer to industrial greywater using time-aligned, stage-by-stage sampling, matrix-recovery checks and independent reference measurements, then use flow-aware metal balances to distinguish measurement effects from actual metal release or accumulation.

rationale.text: He has directly relevant experience evaluating portable manganese methods against reference measurements, including identifying hardness-dependent interference.

sources.quote: In high-hardness matrix, the periodate procedure showed a positive bias of 7–13% on the absorbance platforms
results from the formaldoxime absorbance method agreed with ICP-OES reference values within 4.5%.

rationale.text: His iron-speciation work can inform sampling protocols that distinguish genuine process changes from preservation and precipitation artefacts.

sources.quote: This study combined field Eh and pH measurements with laboratory Fe(II), Fe(III), and total iron determinations by ICP-OES and spectrophotometry
Fe(III) precipitation within 5 minutes of sampling accounted for losses of 12–38% of total iron from the dissolved fraction.

rationale.text: He has translated interference-correction research into practical tools and harmonised protocols for water-sector operators.

sources.quote: The models were implemented in a freely downloadable spreadsheet calculator and in a printed field reference card distributed to water utility technicians in three municipalities.
Radulović led the work package on matrix interference assessment, contributing the iron, manganese, and phosphate correction procedures developed in his laboratory.

rationale.text: His laboratory has instrumentation relevant to independent analytical checks, and his stated collaboration interests include applied water-quality measurement problems.

sources.quote: The group operates a small field-analytical laboratory equipped with portable spectrophotometers, ion chromatography, ICP-OES, and a titration workstation.
Radulović is primarily interested in applied collaborations where his interference correction models and groundwater matrix expertise can solve a specific measurement problem

constraints.text: Use the company-reported discharge limits of 0.10 mg/L manganese and 0.30 mg/L iron as provisional acceptance criteria, subject to verifying the applicable regulation and compliance sampling requirements.

sources.quote: Serbian regulation SR-IED-2023 lowered the allowable manganese in treated discharge to 0.10 mg/L and iron to 0.30 mg/L.

constraints.text: Complete diagnosis and an implementable intervention within the four-month company staffing window, leaving time before the five-month reinspection.

sources.quote: can dedicate two senior process engineers and one lab technician to a defined project for up to four months
one large laundry client faces a reinspection in five months.

constraints.text: Any proposed remedy must work at existing installations without major equipment replacement.

sources.quote: a root-cause finding with a specific process change we can implement at existing installations without replacing major equipment.

constraints.text: Build the investigation around accessible process-stage samples and the three available installations; preserve cross-site comparisons rather than assuming one site's cause explains all failures.

sources.quote: We have on-site analytical kit and can pull samples at every process stage.
with access to three operating installations for field testing.
0.18 mg/L manganese at the outlet of our coagulation stage across three different client sites.

constraints.text: Treat external confirmation and the unsuccessful dose/pH trials as baseline evidence: do not presume a photometric artefact or simply repeat these adjustments as the proposed solution.

sources.quote: Our own analysers, confirmed by an accredited external lab in Zrenjanin
increasing coagulant dose by 30 percent and dropping pH from 7.4 to 6.9 during coagulation, without meaningful improvement.

risks: The manganese and iron methods were demonstrated principally in groundwater, not industrial laundry or food-processing greywater. Industrial matrix effects and analyte recovery must be tested in the first experiment before applying the published corrections.

External laboratory confirmation makes a purely on-site instrument-bias explanation insufficient without new evidence; the cause may instead involve real metal inputs, filter-media release, tank cycling or recirculation.

The supplied evidence establishes analytical and sampling expertise more strongly than treatment-process remediation expertise. Confirmed media or tank-related release may require an additional process specialist.
Researcher availability and committed laboratory capacity remain unknown. The general note about availability from 2025 onward does not establish capacity for this four-month project.
The budget, site operating restrictions, actual iron concentrations and legally applicable analytical definitions are unknown; these could prevent a timely or affordable intervention.
Unaligned inlet and outlet samples, changing flow or recycle streams could create a misleading apparent manganese increase unless sampling follows hydraulic residence times and metal balances.
questions: Can Radulović commit to the required four-month investigation, including early fieldwork, reference analyses and rapid reporting, and does he accept a scope extending from measurement validation to joint root-cause diagnosis?
What budget is available for sampling, reference laboratory work, media and reagent testing, and controlled operational trials?
What discharge permit and regulatory text apply, and do the limits concern total, dissolved or another defined metal fraction? What sampling and analytical methods will the reinspection accept?
What are the actual iron results, and can AquaCikl provide raw on-site and external laboratory reports, methods, detection limits, preservation records and quality-control results?

Can the company provide process diagrams, flows, recycle routes, hydraulic residence times, dosing records, media histories and tank cleaning/redox records to support time-aligned sampling and metal balances?

Can the first experiment include paired field/reference measurements, matrix spikes, appropriately preserved total and dissolved fractions, and samples of candidate metal inputs such as coagulants and filter media?

What operational changes and temporary isolation tests are permitted at each site, and who will provide treatment-process expertise if confirmed metal release requires work beyond analytical diagnosis?
